app.name: SnailNet
link.not_running.title: SnailNet isn't running
link.not_running.body: Your internet works normally, but nothing is being shared out. SnailNet connects by itself as soon as its service starts.
start.asked: Starting SnailNet… it connects in a moment.
start.cancelled: SnailNet wasn't started. Windows needs your permission to start it.
start.not_installed: The SnailNet service isn't installed on this PC. Reinstall SnailNet to get it back.
offline.title: No internet connection
offline.body: This PC isn't connected to a network. SnailNet keeps your split and picks up as soon as you're back online.
link.rejected.title: This copy of SnailNet can't control the service
link.rejected.body: Only the SnailNet app installed in the same folder as the service may change it. Open SnailNet from the Start menu instead.
link.denied.title: Windows didn't let SnailNet reach its service
link.denied.body: Signing out and back in usually fixes this. Details: {detail}
link.lost.title: Lost contact with SnailNet
link.lost.body: Reconnecting… Your internet keeps working meanwhile.
state.unshaped.title: Watching only
state.unshaped.body: Tell SnailNet how fast your connection is, and it starts sharing it out by your rules.
state.retrying.title: Traffic control stepped aside
state.retrying.body: Your internet works normally. SnailNet tries again in a moment. ({reason})
state.safe_mode.title: Safe mode
state.safe_mode.body: Traffic control stopped after {failures} problems in a row, so your internet runs as if SnailNet weren't here. Restart the SnailNet service to try again.
network.new.title: New network: {network}
network.new.body: SnailNet doesn't know this connection's speed yet, so it's only watching. Set or measure it once, and your split works here too.
line.title: Connection speed
line.body: Type the speeds a speed test shows for this connection. SnailNet shares it out at these speeds.
line.empty: Leave a box empty and SnailNet won't share out that direction.
line.invalid: Type a number from 0.1 to 10000, or leave it empty.
line.conflict: The settings changed somewhere else just now. This shows the new speeds; try again.
firstrun.label: Welcome
firstrun.welcome.title: Welcome to SnailNet
firstrun.welcome.body: Split your internet between apps, like 40% for downloads and 60% for YouTube.
firstrun.welcome.privacy: SnailNet only reads website names, never content, and nothing leaves your PC.
firstrun.speed.title: How fast is your connection?
firstrun.speed.body: SnailNet can measure it in about 30 seconds with Cloudflare's speed test, or you can type it. You can change it any time.
firstrun.done.title: You're set
firstrun.done.body: SnailNet is sharing out your connection. Pick a mode for what you're doing, or boost one app when it matters. A share nobody is using goes to whoever needs it.
firstrun.later.title: Watching only, for now
firstrun.later.body: Your internet works as before. When you know your speed, choose Set speed at the top of the window.
split.label: How your internet is shared
list.empty.title: No traffic yet
list.empty.body: Apps show up here as soon as they use the internet.
list.unknown: Traffic SnailNet couldn't tie to an app
editor.conflict: The rules changed somewhere else just now. This shows the new version; try again.
picker.title: Add an app or website
picker.hint: Everything here already has a share. Apps show up once they've used the internet.
status.lending: not using all of its share
status.borrowing: also using {mbps} Mbps of spare speed
fix.give.label: Give {name} {pct} percent of your internet in this mode
fix.grow.label: Make {name}'s share {pct} percent in this mode
fix.later.label: Not now: don't suggest this again today
fix.draft: To fix it with one click, save or discard your changes first.
fix.stale: The split changed in the meantime, so nothing was undone.
fix.setting.title: Suggest a fix when an app waits
fix.setting.body: A button on Now, never a pop-up.
glance.quiet.title: Nothing is using your internet right now.
glance.quiet.body: Apps show up here as soon as they do.
glance.top.calm: {name} is using the most right now.
glance.top.busy: {name} is using most of your internet.
glance.room: {used} of {line} Mbps in use. There's plenty left.
glance.borrow.from: It's using speed {lender} doesn't need right now.
glance.borrow.spare: It's using speed nobody else needs.
glance.held: SnailNet keeps it to its share.
glance.alone: Nothing else needs your internet right now.
strip.free: {mbps} Mbps held back to keep ping low
dir.label: Show speeds for
row.members: These apps have no share of their own. Click one to give it one.
edit.priority.hint: High priority sends its data first, which keeps games and calls responsive. It doesn't make the share bigger.
edit.site: Works in every browser, and counts before the browser's own share.
nav.label: Pages
sidebar.line.label: Internet speed: {down} Mbps download, {up} Mbps upload. Change it
mode.label: Mode
settings.hotkey.body: Press it anywhere to switch to the next mode.
settings.hotkey.taken: Another program already uses {keys}, so SnailNet can't.
settings.hotkey.kept: Another program already uses {keys}, so SnailNet kept {kept}.
settings.metered: This network is metered. A speed test uses about 30 seconds of data: it downloads once more at the end to check ping with SnailNet.
first.done.game: {name} counts as a game now: it goes first while it runs.
first.list.title: Apps you marked
first.list.body: Games and "never first", from their Boost menu.
first.list.remove.label: Let SnailNet decide for {name}
mode.copy.name: {mode} copy
mode.copy.done: Made “{mode}”. Changes on this page now go into the copy.
mode.rename.title: Rename this mode
mode.rename.label: Name
mode.delete.title: Delete “{mode}”?
mode.delete.body: Its split goes with it. If it's on, Balanced takes over.
mode.playing.note: Gaming mode while you play. {mode} comes back when the game closes.
mode.balanced.body: Every app gets a fair share.
mode.streaming.body: Videos and calls stay smooth. Downloads wait.
mode.gaming.body: Your game and voice chat come first.
mode.quiet.body: Downloads never slow anything else down.
who.title: Using your internet
who.amount.big: a big part of your speed
unnamed.body: from websites that hide their names, in {apps}. It still counts toward those apps' shares.
who.empty: Nothing is using your internet right now. Apps show up here as soon as they do.
boost.label: Boost {name}
boost.stop.label: Stop boosting {name}
proof.note: {name} is filling your internet, and games and calls still feel it as {now} ms.
proof.none: Run a speed test to see how much your ping goes up while something downloads.
boost.menu.title: Let {name} go first
boost.menu.body: It gets at least half your speed. Everything goes back to normal by itself.
split.title: {mode} split
split.reset.done: The {mode} split is back to how it started.
settings.title: Settings
settings.networks.body: Each network remembers its own speed. SnailNet switches by itself when you join one.
measure.done: Measured {down} Mbps down and {up} Mbps up. SnailNet now shares that out.
measure.none: The speed test didn't finish. Check that you're online, or type your speed with Change.
measure.checking: Checking ping with SnailNet… about 10 seconds
measure.done.proof: Measured {down} Mbps down and {up} up. While downloading, ping was {without} ms without SnailNet and {with} ms with it.
proof.live: Ping {now} ms while {name} fills your internet
proof.sr: Ping {now} ms with SnailNet; {without} ms without it at your last speed test.
proof.grade.what: How much your ping goes up while something downloads. A means you won't notice; F means games and calls will lag.
proof.grade.calm: Your internet keeps ping low on its own.
adapt.title: Adjust to my speed by itself
adapt.body: Follows your internet when it gets faster or slower. Off keeps the speed you set.
focus.title: The app you're using
focus.body: The window in front, or a running game. First, never more.
gaming.title: Gaming mode while you play
gaming.body: Back to your mode when the game closes.
calls.title: Calls
calls.body: A voice or video call, in any app or browser, while it lasts.
state.measuring.title: Measuring your connection
state.measuring.body: Sharing is off for about 20 seconds so the test can use the whole line.
autostart.ask.title: Start SnailNet with Windows?
autostart.ask.body: It waits quietly in the tray and keeps sharing your internet from the moment you sign in. You can change this in Settings any time.
settings.resetMode.body: Other modes stay as they are.
settings.resetAll.body: Every mode, your speed and any boost; then setup again.
settings.resetAll.title: Reset SnailNet?
settings.resetAll.confirm: Every mode goes back to how it started and your internet speed is cleared, so SnailNet only watches until you set it again. This can't be undone.
packs.title: Keep app and game lists up to date
packs.body: Newer lists from GitHub once a day, so new apps and games are known. Nothing about you is sent.
settings.update.body: SnailNet checks by itself when it starts.
settings.update.available: SnailNet {version} is out. Updating restarts SnailNet; your internet keeps working.
settings.update.failed: Couldn't check for updates. Try again later.
who.game.fullscreen: Goes first · a game, it ran full screen
who.game.library: Goes first · a game, in a launcher's library
who.game.marked: Goes first · you said it's a game
state.paused.title: SnailNet is paused
state.paused.body: Nothing is shared out or blocked, so your internet runs as if SnailNet weren't here. Back on: {left}.
pause.label: Pause SnailNet
pause.menu.body: Nothing is shared out or blocked while it's paused.
group.back: Put it back with its app
group.merge: Count it as part of another app
group.split.done: {exe} is an app of its own now, out of {app}.
group.separate.done: {name} is an app of its own again.
group.failed: Couldn't change how apps are grouped. {message}
group.list.title: How apps are grouped
group.list.body: Programs you split off or merged, from Boost menus.
group.list.back.label: Put {name} back into its app
group.list.separate.label: Make {name} an app of its own again
block.title: Blocked
block.unblock.label: Let {name} use the internet again
fold.title: {count} apps that only use spare speed
fold.title.one: 1 app that only uses spare speed
now.heading: Your internet right now
now.noslices: {mode} doesn't guarantee any app a share yet.
split.intro: When your internet is busy, each app here still gets at least its share. Whatever it doesn't use goes to the others.
split.empty.title: No app has a guaranteed share yet
split.empty.body: Right now every app competes for speed. Pick what you don't want interrupted, like a game, a video or a call, and it always gets its share, even while something big downloads.
split.other.hint: Apps without a share of their own split this. It always keeps at least 5%.
edit.free.hint: No guaranteed share: it only uses speed nobody else needs. Good for updates and big downloads.
edit.limit.hint: Never faster than this, even when nothing else is using the internet.
edit.remove.hint: Its share goes back to the other apps.
bar.label: Drag to change the split
row.was.label: {name} was {pct} percent before your changes
draft.title: Unsaved changes
draft.conflict: Someone else changed the split just now. Press Save again to keep yours.
draft.invalid: These shares don't add up. Discard them and try again.
draft.stale.title: The split changed somewhere else
draft.stale.body: Since you started, the split was changed from the tray or by a mode switch.
leave.title: Save your changes to the {mode} split?
leave.body: They aren't in use yet. If you don't save them, they're lost.
more.label: More for {name}
proof.quiet: How much ping goes up while something downloads. Live ping shows here when your internet gets busy.
fix.why: At least {mbps} Mbps whenever it needs it
flyout.grades: Quiet right now. Ping grade {with} with SnailNet, {without} without.
